title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration
summary: Hold: the migration command combines two separate operations into an invalid call, and the shared-data licensing statement omits Enterprise Agreement eligibility. The page also overstates one-way migration and redirects, incorrectly excludes source administrators from standalone migration commands, and schedules security-group preparation too late.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Migration requires source-to-target identity mapping.
claims.quote: Identity Mapping is required, which means the specific user configuration supported by Identity Mapping is required.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant migration requires establishing trust between the tenants.
claims.quote: To establish trust, each SharePoint tenant administrator must run specific commands on both source and target tenants.

claims.claim: Security groups need preparation or recreation in the target tenant.
claims.quote: Precreate users and groups as needed in the target tenant's directory. ... Precreated users must be added as members of any appropriate security groups or unified groups before the OneDrive migration begins.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-onedrive-migration-step4 and describe target group and membership preparation before migration.

claims.claim: Some associated objects need rebuilding during migration.
claims.quote: Workflows (2010 or 2013) must be re-created and republished on the Target tenant. ... PowerApps and Automation Tasks must be recreated and reconnected to the Site on the target tenant.
claims.fix: Name SharePoint workflows and Power Apps/automation tasks as the examples and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-sharepoint-migration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Cross-tenant moves generally are one-way.
claims.quote: Move mailboxes back to the original source ... If a mailbox is required to move back to the original source tenant, the same set of steps and scripts must be run in both new source and new target tenants, with some variance.
claims.fix: Limit the one-and-done wording to existing OneDrive and SharePoint migration, citing their migration overviews. Remove the blanket one-way assertion from the risk rationale; mailbox migration documents moving back to the original source.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant moves generally leave redirects behind.
claims.quote: Chats and meetings are migrated from the source to the target. The original content on the source remains, though it might be in an edited form.
claims.fix: Say that OneDrive and SharePoint moves leave redirect links, rather than applying redirect behaviour to every workload. The orchestrator overview says original Teams content remains in the source.

claims.claim: OneDrive migration does not support incremental or delta passes.
claims.quote: The OneDrive content moves from the source to the target, leaving behind a redirect link on the source. Incremental and delta migration passes can't be performed.

claims.claim: SharePoint migration does not support incremental or delta passes.
claims.quote: Incremental and delta migration passes can't be performed.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-sharepoint-migration to sources and scope this limitation to the existing SharePoint tool.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin UI for creating, validating and running orchestrator migration batches.
claims.quote: Searched: "migration orchestrator" "admin center" "migration batch" UI portal. Opened Running the migration and orchestrator overview; only Graph/PowerShell/Graph Explorer instructions found, not an orchestrator admin-centre path.

claims.claim: The slash-combined Test-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob / Move-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob expression creates, validates and runs a batch.
claims.quote: Test-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <batch display name or job id> ... Once the batch status is ValidatePassed, call migrate ... Move-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <batch display name or job id>
claims.fix: Retain Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'CrossTenantContentMigration.ReadWrite.All'. Print Test-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <id> and Move-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <id> separately, requiring ValidatePassed before Move. Rename the row 'Validating and running an existing migration batch', or add creation using New-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob with the documented body/settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin UI for SharePoint and OneDrive cross-tenant migration trust.
claims.quote: Searched: cross tenant SharePoint OneDrive migration establish trust admin center UI Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship. Opened SharePoint trust step 2 and OneDrive overview; read OneDrive trust search excerpts. Only PowerShell trust setup found.

claims.claim: Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship -Scenario MnA -PartnerRole Target -PartnerCrossTenantHostUrl <url> requests trust with the target tenant.
claims.quote: On the source tenant, run this command to send a trust request to the target tenant: Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship -Scenario MnA -PartnerRole Target -PartnerCrossTenantHostUrl <TARGETCrossTenantHostUrl>
claims.fix: Note that the printed call runs on the source and is one half of trust setup. Also give the target-side call: Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship -Scenario MnA -PartnerRole Source -PartnerCrossTenantHostUrl <source-host-url>, as the cited page documents.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin UI for the existing cross-tenant OneDrive move.
claims.quote: Searched: cross tenant OneDrive SharePoint site content move admin UI portal PowerShell. Opened OneDrive migration overview and step 6; only SharePoint Online PowerShell move instructions found.

claims.claim: Start-SPOCrossTenantUserContentMove with SourceUserPrincipalName, TargetUserPrincipalName and TargetCrossTenantHostUrl starts a user's OneDrive move.
claims.quote: Start-SPOCrossTenantUserContentMove -SourceUserPrincipalName <...> -TargetUserPrincipalName <...> -TargetCrossTenantHostUrl <...>

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin UI for the existing cross-tenant SharePoint site move.
claims.quote: Searched: cross tenant OneDrive SharePoint site content move admin UI portal PowerShell. Opened SharePoint migration overview and step 6; only SharePoint Online PowerShell site-move instructions found.

claims.claim: Start-SPOCrossTenantSiteContentMove is the documented cmdlet for moving a SharePoint site.
claims.quote: Start-SPOCrossTenantSiteContentMove -SourceSiteUrl <...> -TargetSiteUrl <...> -TargetCrossTenantHostUrl <...>
claims.fix: Give the useful documented call: Start-SPOCrossTenantSiteContentMove -SourceSiteUrl <source-site-url> -TargetSiteUrl <target-site-url> -TargetCrossTenantHostUrl <target-host-url>. Note that a source-tenant SharePoint Admin or Microsoft 365 Global Admin runs it.

claims.where: controls[4].ui, controls[4].api, controls[4].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: A distinct admin-centre page and its automation surface for the roadmap experience are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "migration orchestrator" "admin center" "migration batch" UI portal; "Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration" licensing price admin center API. Opened orchestrator overview and Running the migration; existing Graph tooling found, no distinct admin-centre page.

claims.claim: The documented orchestrator uses Graph APIs callable through Graph PowerShell or Graph Explorer rather than a documented migration admin-centre workflow.
claims.quote: Migrations are managed through Graph APIs. These APIs can be run with PowerShell 5 or 7, or with Graph Explorer.

claims.claim: The standalone SharePoint and OneDrive migration cmdlets use SharePoint Online Management Shell.
claims.quote: Microsoft SharePoint Online Powershell. Confirm you have the most recent version installed. Download SharePoint Online Management Shell from the official Microsoft Download Center.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-onedrive-migration and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-sharepoint-migration to sources for their tooling prerequisites.

claims.claim: Source tenants cannot run the migration commands, without a qualification limiting this to orchestrator commands.
claims.quote: To start the migration, a SharePoint Admin or Microsoft 365 Global Admin of the source tenant must run the following command: Start-SPOCrossTenantUserContentMove
claims.fix: Replace with: 'Orchestrator Graph migration commands run from the target tenant. The standalone OneDrive and SharePoint move commands in this table run from the source tenant as a SharePoint Admin or Microsoft 365 Global Admin.' Both cited step-6 pages document the source-side role.

claims.claim: Orchestrator validation results expire after seven days.
claims.quote: Validation must pass within the last seven days. If more than seven days elapsed since validation passed, you must revalidate before migrating.

claims.claim: Rebuilding security groups is an after-rollout preparation step.
claims.quote: Precreate users and groups as needed in the target tenant's directory. ... Precreated users must be added as members of any appropriate security groups or unified groups before the OneDrive migration begins.
claims.fix: Move group preparation to Before rollout: 'Precreate target security groups, populate memberships and include them in identity mapping before migrating content.' After rollout, verify memberships and permissions instead of first rebuilding groups.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits this optional admin-opt-in migration capability.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; defaultState: "admin-opt-in". The assessment scale assigns review when nothing changes until an administrator chooses an optional capability.
claims.fix: Set action to review: the documented process requires administrative setup and explicit batch submission, with no supplied mandatory deadline or automatic content migration.

claims.claim: The controls table covers the operational controls named in the governance checklist.
claims.quote: The checklist says 'Plan identity mapping, licences in the target tenant and holds' and 'Rebuild security groups'; the table has batch execution, trust, workload moves and an admin-page gap, but no preparation or hold-check rows.
claims.fix: Add rows covering identity mapping, licence assignment and hold checks, and target group preparation; combine directly related preparation controls if needed. Cite the documented surfaces rather than assuming null, and move group preparation before migration.

claims.claim: Final licensing specifically for the roadmap orchestrated experience remains unpublished.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration" licensing price admin center API. Opened orchestrator overview and SharePoint migration overview; found existing user and shared-data licensing, not final terms identifying the new roadmap admin-centre experience.
